title: Unix signals are a doorbell, not a message
body: A signal tells a process that something happened but carries almost no information and can coalesce: send three SIGCHLDs quickly and a parent may observe one notification for several dead children. Correct handlers therefore just set a flag and let the main loop do the work. Treating signals as a rich channel is a reliable bug generator.
source_hint: POSIX signal semantics; signal-safety man pages
